findings.claim: The context enters the fourth-constraint residual ONLY as an additive constant: c3 = sigma0(W4) + W3 + K_ctx exactly, with K_ctx a single 32-bit constant per context. Consequence (the analytic result of this lens): a per-context cost difference is mathematically IDENTICAL to non-uniformity of the pooled, context-free variable S = W3 + sigma0(W4), because P(c3=0 | ctx) = P(S = -K_ctx). Context screening, representative-policy steering, and 'is c3 uniform' are therefore one single question, not three, and all 40 contexts have exactly the same c3 distribution up to a shift by construction.
findings.evidence: c3 - sigma0(W4) - W3 has exactly 1 distinct value inside each of the 40 contexts and exactly 40 distinct values overall, over all 68,680 rows (L4_main check; K_ctx = 04270d0c, 9c1eb9e6, adada9b4, ...). Alternatives sigma1(W4)+W3 and sigma0(W3)+W4 give 68,152 distinct residuals, i.e. no structure. Also verified sigma0 is GF(2)-BIJECTIVE (rank 32 over GF(2), computed from its 32 basis images), so sigma0(W4) is uniform iff W4 is.
findings.effect_if_real: Collapses lens items (a), (c) and (d) into a single testable statement, and makes the screening campaign's target well defined: screening contexts can only work if the pooled distribution of S = W3 + sigma0(W4) has a measurable peak, since the only per-context freedom is which point -K_ctx you land on.

findings.claim: S = W3 + sigma0(W4) (equivalently c3 with the context shift removed) is uniform on Z_2^32 to the limit of the corpus, under a Fourier scan over 8.39 million frequencies with a validated positive control. No steerable residual bias exists at any scale this data can see.
findings.evidence: Fourier/characteristic-function scan of the empirical distribution of S over Z_2^32 (histogram of S>>8 into 2^24 bins, rFFT): statistic 2n|chat(t)|^2 (~Exp, mean 2 under uniformity), max over T=8,388,607 frequencies = 30.40, against E[max] = 2 ln T = 31.88; zero frequencies exceed threshold. Same at 2^20 bins (26.32 vs 26.34) and 2^16 bins (18.09 vs 20.79). POSITIVE CONTROL on the known-biased W3: max statistic 3235.07 at t=1, i.e. 100x over threshold, so the test unambiguously has power. Also: 209 moduli m (3..200 plus 251,257,641,1021,4093,65535,65537,16843009,3*5*17*257) -> max |z| = 2.64 (m=125) against expected max 3.47; low-k chi2 for k=8/12/16 z = +0.12/-2.00/+0.32; collision counts on low 16/20/24 bits z = +1.56/-0.38/-1.23; full-32 collisions 1 observed vs 0.541 expected.
findings.effect_if_real: Negative. Rules out residue-class, multiplicative and coset structure in c3 at the measurable scale; the 2^-32 filter is flat and the 2^45.4 cost estimate stands.

findings.claim: No context effect. The 40 contexts are statistically indistinguishable in every measure tried, so there are no systematically cheap contexts to screen for at any effect size this corpus can resolve.
findings.evidence: Deduped n=68,152, ~1,700/context. ctx x low-k(c3) contingency chi2: k=4 z=-0.45, k=6 z=+0.62, k=8 z=+0.79; ctx x (c3 mod m) for m=3/5/17/257 z = +0.30/+1.64/-0.12/+2.61 (pre-dedup). Per-context mean(c3): max|z| = 2.69 over 40 (expected max ~2.5). Per-context low-12-bit chi2 spread: min z = -1.02, max z = +1.60 across 40 contexts. Per-context zero-ladder counts (the quantity that actually matters): low-3==0 dispersion chi2 = 33.1/df 39 (z=-0.67), low-4==0 chi2 = 38.7/df 39 (z=-0.03), low-5==0 chi2 = 36.6/df 39 (z=-0.27). No dependence on the free word v either: corr(popcount(v), per-ctx mean-c3 z) = -0.110 (sd 0.164, n=40); max |corr(bit j of v, per-ctx P(c3 bit i))| = 0.439 over 1024 pairs, expected max ~0.575.
findings.effect_if_real: Negative. Per-context screening at R=20 is dead down to a per-context inflation factor of about 1.27 on the low-3-bit class (4 sigma); anything smaller is invisible with ~1,700 candidates/context and would need ~100x more data per context to test.

findings.claim: Changing the table's representative policy CANNOT change P(c3 = 0) — this is provable from the decomposition, not merely unobserved. W3 carries a large, forced max-representative bias (P(bit31)=0.6213, 0.057 bits lost) and that bias is entirely absorbed by the modular addition of sigma0(W4), which is uniform and independent of W3. Policy changes buy candidate YIELD only, never per-candidate success probability.
findings.evidence: c3 = W3 + sigma0(W4) + K_ctx with mod-2^32 addition. sigma0(W4) measured uniform (per-bit max |p-0.5| = 0.00483 vs 4sd = 0.00766; low-8/12/16-bit chi2 z = -1.00/+0.38/+0.20; Fourier scan max stat 33.30 vs E[max] 31.88, i.e. +1.1 sd of the max distribution). W3 and sigma0(W4) independent: 32x32 bit-agreement max |z| = 3.15 over 1024 tests, 0 exceed 4; W3-top-4-bits x low-8/low-12 of sigma0(W4) contingency z = +0.60/-1.25. Bitwise entropies: W3 = 31.9430, sigma0(W4) = 31.999573, c3 = 31.999701 bits. Adding a uniform independent summand mod 2^32 yields an exactly uniform sum for ANY distribution of W3.
findings.effect_if_real: Negative but decisive for lens item (c): the ~4x reachability gain from storing all roots instead of the max root is purely a yield gain (4x more candidates per swept a0), with zero change to the 2^-32 filter. Do not expect a policy change to reduce the 2^45.4 exponent.

findings.claim: c3 is not predictable, at any low-order approximation, from a0 or from the intermediate lookup outputs W1/W2 — so there is no early-abort after lookup 1 or 2, and no pre-lookup predictor.
findings.evidence: 12.7 million hypothesis tests, all consistent with noise. (i) Low-weight GF(2) linear test, masks of weight<=3 on a0 x weight<=2 on c3: 2,897,664 tests, max|z| = 5.18 against max-of-Gaussians threshold 5.58; repeated against S instead of c3 (correct context pooling): max|z| = 5.00. (ii) Weight<=2 x weight<=2 masks of each of a0, W1, W2, W3, W4 against c3 (5 x 278,784 tests): max|z| = 4.60/4.77/5.16/4.53/4.81 against threshold 5.14, and #|z|>4 = 18/10/20/19/10 against 17.6 expected. (iii) a0-sorted nearest-neighbour autocorrelation within context (68,112 pairs): P(c3 bit agrees) max|z| = 2.70, zero bits above 3 sigma; Pearson lag-1/2/3/5/10 pooled z = -1.47/+1.17/+0.46/+0.77/-0.66. (iv) (a0 mod m) x (c3 mod m) for m = 3,5,7,16,17,256: max z = +3.35 (m=256, df=65025). Note a0 survivors are sparse (median gap 1.75e6), so only long-range a0 structure is testable.
findings.effect_if_real: Negative. Confirms the brief's assumption that the residual behaves as a flat 2^-32 filter that must be paid after all three lookups.

findings.claim: Both corpora contain exactly-duplicated rows: 528 of 68,680 rows in corpus_r20 (0.77%) and 205 of 51,268 in corpus_r19 (0.40%). These are identical (ctx, a0, a1..a3, W0..W4, e0..e3, c3) records, i.e. the same swept a0 emitted two or three times, uniformly spread over all 40 (resp. 57/60) contexts and over the a0 range. They are a pipeline artifact, not a cryptanalytic property, but they silently corrupt any collision- or coincidence-based statistic.
findings.evidence: np.unique over the full row tuple: r20 68,680 -> 68,152 distinct, multiplicity histogram [67626 singles, 524 doubles, 2 triples]; r19 51,268 -> 51,063 distinct, [50859, 203, 1]. distinct (ctx,a0) equals distinct full rows in both, so the duplication is at the (ctx,a0) level. Concrete damage: BEFORE dedup, exact 32-bit c3 collisions were 531 against 0.549 expected (a spurious ~700-sigma 'signal'), low-24-bit collisions z = +43.73, and the a0-neighbour autocorrelation showed a fake max|z| = 4.70. AFTER dedup all of these vanish (32-bit collisions 1 vs 0.541 expected; low-24 z = -1.23; neighbour max|z| = 2.70). Duplicate a0 values are flat across the top-4-bit histogram, so this is not a boundary effect of a single tile.
findings.effect_if_real: About 0.4-0.8% of swept a0 in the production search is being processed twice (overlapping sweep ranges or a double-emit in the candidate writer) — a small free saving. More importantly, any past or future project statistic based on distinct-candidate counts, collision counts, or near-neighbour coincidence must dedupe first or it will manufacture large false signals.

detection_power: Corpus deduped to n = 68,152 (see finding 6); all numbers below are post-dedup. Baseline sensitivities: per-bit bias sd = 0.00192, so a per-bit deviation below 0.0077 (4 sigma) is invisible; a single Fourier/character magnitude |chat(t)| below 0.0149 is invisible. Multiple-testing was handled by comparing the observed maximum to the expected maximum of the null order statistic, not by a per-test threshold: for the GF(2) linear scans, threshold sqrt(2 ln 2T) (5.14 for T=278,784; 5.58 for T=2,897,664); for the Fourier scans, 2 ln T on the Exp(2)-distributed statistic (31.88 for T=8.39e6). Total tests run: ~12.7 million (2.90M weight<=3 GF(2) masks, 1.39M weight<=2 cross-masks, 8.39M Fourier frequencies, 209 moduli, ~2,000 contingency/ladder tests). Every family's maximum fell at or below its expected maximum. Test validity was confirmed by a positive control: the same Fourier scan applied to W3, whose max-representative bias is known and forced, returns statistic 3235 against threshold 32 (100x), and W3's per-bit z reaches +63.3 at bit 31 — so the machinery detects real structure of this magnitude immediately. Economic power, i.e. what speedup would have been seen: a GLOBAL inflation of P(c3 = 0 mod 2^k) is detectable at 4 sigma down to factor 1.061 at k=4, 1.245 at k=8, 1.98 at k=12; a PER-CONTEXT inflation (n~1,700/context) down to factor 1.27 at k=3, 1.39 at k=4, 1.55 at k=5. So a factor-2-or-better lever of any of the forms tested would have been unmissable, and a 6% lever on the low-4-bit class would have been caught. HONEST LIMITS, three of them. (1) The residual c3 is a deterministic function of (ctx, a0); the tests search only for a LOW-COMPLEXITY approximation (GF(2)-linear in bits, small-modulus arithmetic, single Fourier mode, nearest-neighbour continuity). A predictor requiring higher algebraic degree or many terms would pass every test here undetected. (2) A speedup carried diffusely by ~2^32 individually-tiny Fourier coefficients is not excluded by any single-frequency scan; only structure concentrated on few modes or on simple sets is ruled out. (3) P(c3 = 0) itself is unobservable: zero of 68,680 candidates have c3 = 0 (expectation 1.6e-5), so every statement about the true cost is an extrapolation from coarse-grained proxies (low-k-bit classes, residue classes, Fourier modes), never a direct measurement of the filter probability. a0 survivors are also sparse within a context (median gap 1.75e6, minimum gap 5), so short-range autocorrelation in a0 below ~2^14 is essentially untested.
headline: The fourth-constraint residual is not steerable, and the reason is structural rather than statistical: c3 = sigma0(W4) + W3 + K_ctx exactly, with the context entering ONLY as an additive constant K_ctx — so "are some contexts cheaper" is mathematically the same question as "is the pooled, context-free variable S = W3 + sigma0(W4) non-uniform", and S is uniform under an 8.4-million-frequency Fourier scan with a validated positive control (max statistic 30.4 vs expected max 31.9; the same scan on the known-biased W3 returns 3235). Corollary that settles lens item (c) by proof rather than measurement: W3 carries the whole forced max-representative bias (0.057 bits, P(bit31)=0.621) and sigma0 is GF(2)-bijective with sigma0(W4) measured uniform and independent of W3, so the modular addition absorbs ANY W3 distribution — changing the table's representative policy cannot move P(c3=0) at all, and the ~4x from storing all roots is a pure yield gain against an unchanged 2^-32 filter. Zero signal from 12.7 million tests over a0-autocorrelation, per-context screening, residue classes, and low-weight GF(2) relations. One real defect found: 528 of 68,680 r20 rows (0.77%) and 205 of 51,268 r19 rows (0.40%) are exact duplicates, which alone manufactured a spurious 531-vs-0.549 32-bit collision excess and a fake 4.7-sigma autocorrelation before dedup.

The entire R=20 context/table lever collapses to one scalar -- 2^32 * max_k P(sigma0(W4)+W3 = k) -- and since sigma0 is a GF(2) bijection that scalar is exactly 1 unless W4 is non-uniform, which the corpus bounds but cannot settle (<=8.8x, 95%). The one lever still open and invisible to both corpora is the multi-root table, worth exactly coverage^-3 = 3.93x = 1.97 bits, with the tables already built on disk. Warning: 530 of the 531 apparent X-collisions in corpus_r20 are resampled a0, a trap that yields a fake 2^10 "finding" for anyone who does not dedupe on (ctx,a0).

findings.claim: The R=20 fourth-constraint residual factors exactly as c3 = sigma0(W4) + W3 - K3p, where K3p = W19 - s1(W17) - W12 is a per-context constant computable in O(1) BEFORE the sweep. Therefore the entire context-side lever at R=20 is one additive 32-bit offset, and its maximum possible value is 2^32 * max_k P(X=k) with X := sigma0(W4)+W3 the candidate-side quantity. K3p is freely and apparently surjectively steerable by any of a6, a7, a10, a11, so screening contexts on K3p costs O(1) per context: if X had ANY exploitable non-uniformity it would be harvestable for free.
findings.evidence: exlens_01_reduction.py: implied K3p = sigma0(W4)+W3-c3 is constant within all 40/40 contexts, 40 distinct values, zero exceptions. exlens_06_steer.py: varying a11/a10/a7/a6 each gives 20000 distinct K3p in 20000 draws.
findings.effect_if_real: Reduces every proposed 'context effect', 'better v', 'a11 choice' finding at R=20 to a single measurable scalar. Any such finding that is not a claim about the law of X is provably worthless; any that is, is immediately exploitable at zero screening cost.

findings.claim: sigma0, sigma1, Sigma0 and Sigma1 all have GF(2) rank 32, i.e. all four are bijections. Combined with the factorisation above: X = sigma0(W4) + W3 is EXACTLY uniform whenever W4 is uniform, no matter how biased W3 is (convolution with a uniform group element is uniform). W3 is in fact strongly biased -- bit 31 carries +0.121 -- and that bias is provably irrelevant to C3. The whole C3 lever, including any change of table representative policy, reduces to the single question: is W4 non-uniform?
findings.evidence: exlens_05_closure.py: GF(2) ranks 32/32/32/32. exlens_02_c3law.py: W3 max|z| = 63.6 at bit 31 (bias +0.1214), worst 8-bit-window z = 241.7; but X max|z| = 2.45, worst 8-bit window z = 1.38; c3 max|z| = 1.79. A uniform control at the same N gives max|z| = 1.92 and a worst window z of 4.02.
findings.effect_if_real: Closes representative-policy and context-steering as C3 levers analytically, up to W4's uniformity. Redirects all R=20 lever-hunting onto one 32-bit marginal.

findings.claim: TRAP for the other reviewers: 530 of the 531 exact collisions of X = sigma0(W4)+W3 in corpus_r20 are duplicated rows caused by corpus.py drawing a0 with replacement (2^26 draws from 2^32 per context). The naive reading is 531 collisions against 0.55 expected, i.e. an apparent 2^10 lever. After deduping on (ctx,a0) there is 1 collision against 0.54 expected. The same artefact inflates a0->c3 mutual-information tests: chi2 z falls from +3.35 to +0.69 on the low 8 bits after dedup. corpus_r19 carries 206 such duplicate pairs (predicted 200).
findings.evidence: exlens_03_dupes.py: 68680 rows, 68152 distinct (ctx,a0), 530 duplicate pairs against 536.6 predicted from resampling; X collisions 531 -> 1 after dedup; within-context X collisions after dedup 0 (expected 0.014).
findings.effect_if_real: Any clustering, collision, near-collision, repeated-message or MI finding computed on raw rows from either corpus is invalid. Reviewers must dedupe on (ctx,a0) before reporting.

findings.claim: The largest lever left, and the one both corpora are structurally blind to, is storing the table as a RELATION rather than a function. Measured coverage of the on-disk sigma0(u)-u table is 0.63364, so the one-representative policy discards a factor coverage^-1 = 1.578 of candidates at EACH of the three lookups: exactly 1.975 bits in total. It does not interact with the (3/4)^32 filter, because a3 = W3 - F23 randomises the max-root bias away.
findings.evidence: exlens_04_levers.py: coverage 0.63364 +/- 0.00024 over 4e6 random entries of /nvme0n1-disk/Kamvid/sigma0_u_table.npy; fraction of random u that are the stored representative 0.6345; fraction with stored < u exactly 0.00000, confirming the max policy. exlens_05_closure.py: measured yield/a0 matches coverage^3*(3/4)^32 to 0.9965 +/- 0.0044 (r19) and 1.0012 +/- 0.0038 (r20), so the coverage loss is the whole story.
findings.effect_if_real: R=19: 2^15.26 -> 2^13.29 swept a0 per preimage. R=20: 2^45.4 -> 2^43.43, i.e. 2.45 h -> 37 min on one A100, a 3.93x speedup. sigma0_u_table_root2.npy and sigma0_u_table_root3_refuter1.npy are ALREADY BUILT on disk, so this is a re-run with branching lookups, not a new table build.

findings.claim: The provisional freeze point a2 = a3 = 0 is the unique optimum, exactly rather than empirically. eps = Maj(v,a3,a2) - a3 = Q - P with P = a3&~a2&~v supported on the zero bits of v and Q = a2&~a3&v on the one bits, each bit 1 with probability 1/4 independently. Freezing W9 at any other (a2*,a3*) turns the condition into eps = c* for a nonzero c*, and c = 0 is the strict mode for every v and every width, with the runner-up carrying exactly 1/3 of the mass. Also P(eps=0) = (3/4)^w for every v, so v cannot improve the filter either.
findings.evidence: exlens_04_levers.py: exhaustive enumeration over all (a2,a3) at w = 6, 8, 10 for v = 0, all-ones and a random v. P(eps=0) equals (3/4)^w to six digits in all nine cases; c=0 ranks 1st by mass in all nine; best-other-c mass ratio is exactly 0.3333 in all nine.
findings.effect_if_real: Closes the 'better provisional point' lever exactly, and closes 'choose v to beat (3/4)^32'. Any alternative freeze point costs a factor of 3 (-1.58 bits), taking R=20 from 2.45 h to 7.35 h.

findings.claim: The heavy a4->C0 edge on which the R=20 barrier rests cannot be cut by the submask family's own degeneracy, and this had never been measured inside the family. Tying a8 to a4 to force e8 = 0xFFFFFFFF does remove the Sigma1(e8) route and drops a4->C0 from 12.25 to 8.63 bits, but it turns three previously mild edges heavy: a4->C1 goes 1.62 -> 16.05, a4->C2 goes 1.39 -> 12.91, a4->C3 goes 7.87 -> 12.95. Forcing e8 = e9 = -1 (both a8 and a9 tracking a4) makes all four edges full avalanche (16.26, 15.87, 15.87, 16.06). The family makes the heavy graph strictly worse, not better.
findings.evidence: exlens_04_levers.py, 400 trials per cell, se ~0.40 bits. Harness validated against the published table: the generic frame reproduces the a4 row as 12.25/1.62/1.39/7.87 (paper 12.2/1.7/1.4/7.8) and the a3 control row as 1.65/1.51/7.75/15.31 (paper 1.9/1.6/8.3/15.2).
findings.effect_if_real: Removes the most natural 'the family evades the barrier' hope, and supplies the barrier paper with a measurement it does not currently contain: the family's e8/e9 absorption is a cost, not a cut.

findings.claim: There is no context effect on yield inside the submask family. Per-context candidate counts are Poisson-flat: extra-Poisson relative standard deviation <= 0.35% at R=19 (60 contexts, 95% upper bound) and <= 1.5% at R=20 (40 contexts). Screening the best 10% of contexts on C0/C1/C2 yield is worth at most 1.006x, about 0.009 bits. This is a different regime from the main paper's 3.41x W9-lo-pass screening gain, which was measured for the random-context attack, and that credit should not be carried into the submask-family R=20 estimate.
findings.evidence: exlens_05_closure.py: r19 dispersion chi2 = 50.3 on 59 dof (z = -0.80), sd 27.0 against Poisson 29.2; r20 chi2 = 44.0 on 39 dof (z = +0.57), sd 44.0 against Poisson 41.4. exlens_02_c3law.py: 40x256 independence test of the law of X against context gives z = +1.85 (control +0.22).
findings.effect_if_real: Closes context screening on the candidate-production stage. The only context screening still open at R=20 is screening on K3p, whose value is bounded by the collision test below.

findings.claim: With 68,152 deduped R=20 candidates the corpus can bound but not settle the one remaining C3 question. The 95% Poisson upper bound on collision probability is 2^-28.87 for c3 and 2^-28.46 for W4: the data cannot exclude an additive-steering gain of up to 8.8x, and cannot demonstrate any gain at all (1 collision against 0.54 expected). The decisive experiment has not been run: counting exact X-collisions on N = 4.6e5 deduped candidates brings the bound to ~2x, N = 2e6 to ~1.2x. That is 1.5-7 CPU-hours with corpus.py, or minutes on the existing GPU harness.
findings.evidence: exlens_05_closure.py, deduped N = 68152, uniform expectation 0.54 pairs: collisions W4 = 2, sigma0(W4) = 2, W3 = 3, c3 = 1, uniform control = 0. Per-bit bias of W4 max|z| = 2.41 against a family-wise 5% threshold of 2.93 over 32 bits.
findings.effect_if_real: This is the highest-value un-run experiment at R=20, because the K3p screening that would exploit any excess is free. It is also the correct triage test for any other reviewer's claimed C3 bias: collision entropy of X is the figure of merit, since K3p is effectively uniform across contexts.

findings.claim: COMPLETENESS -- what the two corpora structurally cannot answer, by design. (1) Only one of the five free context words is recorded: v is stored, a6, a7, a10 and a11 are not, so no finding can be attributed to a specific context word. (2) One target per context, 1:1, so target, context and v are perfectly confounded; a per-context effect can never be told from a per-target effect. A crossed design (same context x many targets, same target x many contexts) is required and does not exist. (3) One table only, largest-root policy, so every policy question -- min-root, root2, root3, all-roots -- is invisible. (4) Only rows that PASSED the (3/4)^32 submask filter were kept, so the filter's own pass rate and any dependence of it on v or on table policy is unobservable directly; it can only be inferred from the yield-vs-model ratio. (5) The R=20 corpus was generated in the FILTER frame (a4 = v fixed, C3 used as a 2^-32 test). Frame B of the barrier paper (a4 absorbed by C3 through the global table) is entirely absent, so the corpus says nothing about the absorber corollary's own prediction of a four-absorption R=20 frame.
findings.evidence: Field lists of both npz archives (a0-a3, v, ctx, tgt, c3, W0-W4, e0-e3, messages); corpus.py draws ctx = make_context(rng, R) once per target and stores only a4 as 'v'; TABLE is hard-coded to sigma0_u_table.npy; the mask Maj(v,A3,A2)==A3 is applied before any row is recorded. Confirmed in exlens_01_reduction.py: 40 distinct v, 40 distinct targets, 40 (ctx,tgt) pairs.
findings.effect_if_real: Five named experiments still to run. Cheapest and highest-value: (3), rebuild with root2/all-roots lookups, tables already on disk; and (2), a crossed context x target design at the same cost as the existing corpora.

findings.claim: SCALE-MODEL PREDICTIONS NOT CHECKED AT FULL WIDTH. (i) 'Tables should be relations, not functions': the model measured 1.3%/0%/0% recovery for one representative against 23.4%/6.8%/0.7% for all-roots at w = 4,5,6, an 18x gain at w=4. The full-width structural prediction for the submask family, which has no iteration, is exactly coverage^-3 = 3.93x. Those two numbers disagree by 4.6x and neither has been checked at w = 32. (ii) The accelerating decay of per-a0 success with width (4.15x from w=4 to 5, 8.67x from 5 to 6, the second ratio resting on two events) was never probed at the intermediate widths w = 8, 10, 12 that are still exhaustible and would constrain the functional form the paper says its data cannot constrain. (iii) The phi-family result (W3 = phi(W4) collapses C3 to a one-word absorber) rests on 3-7 events per variant at w=4; at full width my factorisation makes it sharp -- imposing W3 = phi(W4) makes X = sigma0(W4) + phi(W4) a function of one word, whose image covers only ~63% of the range, so the relation costs a further 1.58x on top of the full 32 bits, i.e. strictly worse than the model's 'consistent with 1.0x' counts suggested. (iv) The absorber corollary asserts C3 -> a4 is a global-table absorption giving a 2^32-per-context Frame B; the R=20 attack as actually run does not use it, and my edge measurement shows the submask family cannot host it, since a8 and a9 are defined in terms of a4.
findings.evidence: /home/administrator/sha/publish/paper_r20_barrier.tex lines 278-311 (scale model), 563-583 (absorber corollary), 704-760 (phi-family and elimination orders); coverage measurement and edge-weight tie modes in exlens_04_levers.py.
findings.effect_if_real: Item (i) is the 1.97-bit lever above and should be run first. Item (iii) upgrades a noisy w=4 negative into a full-width structural one worth adding to the paper. Item (iv) is a gap between what the corollary promises and what any code does.

detection_power:
Samples: 51,268 R=19 rows (51,063 after deduping on (ctx,a0); 60 contexts, 60 targets, n_a0 = 2^25 each) and 68,680 R=20 rows (68,152 deduped; 40 contexts, 40 targets, n_a0 = 2^26 each). All figures below are on deduped data, with a matched uniform control of the same size carried through every test; roughly 200 tests were run and all thresholds are Bonferroni-corrected at family-wise 5%.

PER-BIT BIAS: 1 sigma = 0.0019 in probability at N = 68k; family-wise 5% over 32 bits needs |z| > 2.93, so the smallest detectable per-bit bias is 0.0056. Observed maxima: X 2.45, W4 2.41, c3 1.79, uniform control 1.92 -- all null.

WINDOW UNIFORMITY: 8-bit and 12-bit sliding-window chi-squares (25 and 21 tests each) detect a relative RMS non-uniformity of about 3% in an 8-bit marginal. Worst observed on X is z = 1.38 and on c3 z = 2.84, against z = 4.02 for the uniform control -- null. The same test fires at z = 242 on W3, so it has real power and the max-root bias sits exactly where it should.

MUTUAL INFORMATION a0 -> c3: at 6x6 bits the plug-in bias is 0.0417 bits and the estimate 0.0429, so resolution is about 0.04 bits; at 10 bits the plug-in bias (11.0 bits) swamps the estimate and the test is meaningless -- do not run it above 8 bits at this N. findings.claim: The 19-round message blocks have GF(2) affine rank exactly 381 = 512 - 128 - 3 in every one of the 60 contexts. The 128 are the shared W12..W15 tail; the 3 extra relations are the carry-free least-significant bits of the three expansion identities. Nothing else is affinely related.
findings.evidence: Correct nullspace computation over the 38,316 full blocks (my first attempt had a buggy back-substitution and printed garbage masks; DIST_g_rank2.py fixes it). Every context gives rank 381 with 630-640 blocks, so the rank is saturated. The three non-tail relations are identical in all 60 contexts, only the constant changes: W0[0] ^ W1[{3,7,18}] ^ W9[0] = c, W1[0] ^ W2[{3,7,18}] ^ W10[0] = c', W2[0] ^ W3[{3,7,18}] ^ W11[0] = c''. Mask 0x00040088 is exactly {3,7,18} = sigma0's LSB taps, so these are bit 0 of W16 = sigma1(W14)+W9+sigma0(W1)+W0 and its two successors, where bit 0 of an integer sum is an XOR. Per-context constant bits number exactly 128 (the tail) and no more. Scripts/logs: DIST_f_relations.{py,log}, DIST_g_rank2.{py,log}
findings.effect_if_real: Zero exploitable content, but it is a clean statement for the paper: the reachable message set carries no linear structure beyond the two constraints already known.

findings.claim: The table's max-representative bias is confined to the top ~5 bits (P(W[31]=1) = 0.623, then 0.562, 0.531, 0.516, 0.507) and it provably cannot reach the fourth constraint, because sigma0 is a GF(2) bijection and W4 is uniform. Changing the representative policy is a dead lever for the R=20 barrier.
findings.evidence: Corpus marginals for W1, W2, W3 match the table's own stored entries bit-for-bit: 2e7 direct random probes of the on-disk table give stored-root marginals 0.623 / 0.562 / 0.531 / 0.515 / 0.508 / 0.504 / 0.502 / 0.501 and 0.500 thereafter, and mean u / 2^32 = 0.5818. W0 and W4 are flat (max|z| = 2.8). I checked the GF(2) rank of sigma0 by row-reducing its 32x32 matrix: rank 32, i.e. bijective (Sigma0 and sigma1 likewise). Hence s0(W4) is exactly uniform whenever W4 is, and X = s0(W4) + W3 is uniform no matter how W3 is distributed — which is what the data show (X's bit marginals max|z| = 2.4, top-8 chi2 213.0/255 df). Scripts/logs: DIST_b_residual.{py,log}, DIST_l_rank_s0.log

findings.claim: A replicated, previously unlisted within-context bias: sigma0(W2)[31] and sigma0(W3)[31] (equivalently W[6]^W[17]) are biased inside every context, while sigma0(W1)[31] and sigma0(W4)[31] are not. Traced to the max-representative bias of the partner word in the expansion identity. Post-lookup, so worthless as a lever.
findings.evidence: An exhaustive within-context GF(2) scan over the 192 bits (a0, W0..W4), all 192 weight-1 and 18,336 weight-2 masks, statistic T(m) = sum_c S_c(m)^2/n_c ~ chi2(#contexts). After Bonferroni, 35 masks are significant in r19 and 40 in r20; classification: 30 are a0[i]^W0[i] (forced, W0 = a0 + const so this is a carry bit), 3-8 are top bits of W1/W2/W3 (forced, max-representative), and exactly 2 in each corpus are the same two masks — W2[6]^W2[17] (T = 192.3/60 df in r19, 129.6/40 df in r20) and W3[6]^W3[17] (T = 129.6 and 150.1). Note sigma0(x)[31] = x[6]^x[17] identically. The marginal bias is nil (0.5001, 0.4997) — the per-context sign flips — so only a within-context test sees it. Mechanism: W17 = sigma1(W15)+W10+sigma0(W2)+W1 gives sigma0(W2)[31] ^ W1[31] ^ W10[31] ^ carry = const_c, and W1[31] carries the 0.623 max-rep bias; measured within-context corr(sigma0(W2)[31], W1[31]) has sd 0.132 across contexts with mean ~0, and corr(sigma0(W3)[31], W2[31]) sd 0.134. The prediction that sigma0(W1)[31] should show nothing (its partner W0 = a0 + const is uniform) is confirmed: T = 63.2/60 and 49.4/40. With the two forced families removed, the remaining 15,755 weight-2 masks have mean T = 60.13 (H0 60) and 39.98 (H0 40) and only these two exceed threshold. detection_power: Thresholds, stated per family and corrected for multiplicity. (i) Per-bit probabilities in the induced (a2,a3) pattern: 1-sigma 0.0021 (r19) / 0.0018 (r20), so departures from 1/3 above 0.006 / 0.005 are excluded. (ii) Walsh / linear correlations on X, c3 and a0: 1-sigma floor 0.0044 (r19) and 0.0038 (r20); Bonferroni-5% thresholds |z| > 3.16 (32 masks), 3.89 (496), 4.42 (4,960), 4.66 (15,872 cross terms). Every nominal exceedance was retested in the other corpus and none replicated (best cross-corpus follow-up |z| = 2.35). (iii) Mutual information: at 4-bit granularity the 3-sigma MI ceiling is 3.1e-3 bits (H0 mean 2.4e-3); at 6-bit, 4.48e-2 (H0 mean 4.20e-2) — an MI excess above ~2.8e-3 bits would have been seen. (iv) Coarse density of X: 3-sigma bound on RMS relative density deviation is 3.6% (r19) / 3.2% (r20) over 256 bins and ~7% / 6% over 4,096 bins. (v) Absolute yield: 0.9986 +- 0.0029, i.e. +-0.004 bits — the tightest constraint here and the one that closes the (3/4)^32 question. (vi) Per-context yield spread: 95% upper bound 1.5% (r19) / 2.0% (r20). (vii) Within-context weight-2 GF(2) scan: a uniform within-context |corr| >= 0.049 (r19) / 0.037 (r20) would have been detected. Translating the loosest of these into attack terms, the largest speedup this dataset cannot exclude is about 2-4%; nothing near the 2^32 that the fourth constraint costs. Caveat on scope: all tests are marginal or low-order (bit marginals, pairs, triples, 4-6 bit coarse bins, GF(2) linear). A high-degree algebraic relation with no low-order shadow would be invisible to every test run here, and 68,680 samples over a 2^32 residual space cannot see fine-scale density spikes; the yield audit in (v) is the only genuinely global argument, and it constrains the total, not the shape.

headline: Prediction (a) confirmed to 4 decimals: H(a2,a3)=50.7189 vs 32·log2(3)=50.7188, and the surviving pairs are exactly UNIFORM on the 3^32 set — the (3/4)^32 filter is information-theoretically tight, nothing else is constrained. The 20-round residual c3 is indistinguishable from uniform under every test (262,140 exhaustively-scanned frequencies, 17.3M linear approximations, 15,360 bit-bit MI tests): no predictor removes more than ~6e-4 bits. The valuable part is the MECHANISM: c3 = σ0(W4)+W3−K3p is a modular convolution, so φ_c3(β)=φ_W3(β)·φ_σ0(W4)(β). W3 carries a huge 255σ non-uniformity from the maximal-representative policy (|φ_W3(1)|=0.155) and it is annihilated because |φ_σ0(W4)(1)|=0.025 sits at its own noise floor. This is a HARD CAP on lever (c) of the brief: no table representative policy — not even one driving |φ_W3|→1 — can lift |φ_c3(1)| above 0.025, worth ≤9.1e-4 bits. Independently such a policy is exactly zero-sum. Also a methodological warning: the sweep draws a0 WITH REPLACEMENT, and the resulting 530 duplicate rows produce a spectacular +69σ / 6.64-bit FALSE collision signal that vanishes (−1.5σ) on dedup.

The three allowed per-bit states are equiprobable, so the surviving pairs are UNIFORM on the 3^32 allowed set — the (3/4)^32 filter is information-theoretically tight and leaves no residual structure to exploit.

findings.claim: THE MECHANISM, and a hard cap on the brief's lever (c). Because c3 = σ0(W4)+W3−K3p is a sum mod 2^32, its characteristic function factorizes: φ_c3(β)=φ_W3(β)·φ_σ0(W4)(β)·e^(−2πiβK3p/2^32). W3's enormous maximal-representative bias is therefore multiplied by the near-zero coefficient of σ0(W4) and destroyed. Changing the table's representative policy CANNOT beat the fourth constraint, no matter how extreme.
findings.evidence: Measured per-context character magnitudes at β=1 (noise floor 0.0241): |φ_W3|=0.1551 (T=1655.7 against Gamma(40,1), z=+255), |φ_σ0(W4)|=0.0250 (at noise), product 0.00389, observed |φ_c3|=0.0262 — the product law predicts the observation, and it is noise. Same pattern at β=2,3,4,5,8,16,2^16,2^24. Hard cap: even |φ_W3|→1.0 gives |φ_c3(1)| ≤ 0.0250 = at most 9.05e-4 bits. Second, independent reason: a policy storing roots on a density-2^-k subset makes H(W3)=32−k but cuts the table hit rate by 2^-k, so the lookups cost exactly the 2^k the residual would gain — precisely zero-sum. Third, the entire current max-rep bias is only 0.0587 bits, so there was never more than ~0.06 bits available in that direction. Scripts mi_dft.py, mi_conv.py.
findings.effect_if_real: Closes lever (c) of the brief analytically rather than empirically. Corollary for (iii): since φ factorizes, the only route past 2^32 is a JOINT / meet-in-the-middle treatment of σ0(W4)=K3p−W3, not any bias or steering.

A naive within-context collision/birthday statistic on c3 reads +69σ and an apparent 6.64-bit entropy deficit — a complete false positive. Anyone testing this corpus must deduplicate on (ctx,a0) first.

Its TOTAL entropy deficit is only 0.0587 bits, and the same law reproduces the quoted 0.634 lookup hit rate as 1−e^(−1)=0.63212.

Predicted p(bit31=1) = (1−e^(−1/2))/(1−e^(−1)) = 0.62246; measured 0.62292 / 0.62345 / 0.62368 (z=+56 each, spread-inflation across contexts 0.92–1.00, i.e. a genuinely universal bias). Predicted entropy deficit 0.05864 bits vs measured 0.0584 at 4-bit resolution and 0.0586–0.0598 from per-bit sums. The bias lives entirely in the top 4 bits (p = 0.624, 0.557, 0.534, 0.516 for bits 31..28) and the low-bit DFT subgroup is at null (b=4 low: z=+0.67 vs b=4 HIGH: z=+260). findings.evidence: Yield per swept a0 = 0.25258 × (3/4)^32 = 2.537e-5 = 2^(−15.27), independently matching the project's measured 2^(−15.26). Family reach: v,a6,a7,a10 free = 2^128 contexts × 2^32 a0 = 2^160 seeds; in-family preimages available = 2^146.7, reached = 2^144.7, i.e. 2^(−111) of the ~2^256 preimage space of the 19-round compression function — irrelevant in practice since only 2^15.3 seeds are needed per preimage.
