findings.claim: (ii) Exactly 7 affine relations over GF(2) hold on the whole corpus with zero violations — but all 7 are forced trivia: W0−a0 and e0−a0 are a SINGLE global constant across all 100 contexts (they depend only on the IV and K[0]), and the relations are the carry-free low bits of those two additions. No relation survives past bit ~2. No unexplained algebraic structure exists.
findings.evidence: Nullspace of the 449-column bit matrix over {a0,a1,a2,a3,v,W0..W4,e0..e3}: nullity 7, each verified with 0 violations on all 51,268 (R19) and 68,680 (R20) rows. Explanation: W0−a0 = 0x03f777b3 and e0−a0 = 0x9cbf5a55, each taking exactly 1 distinct value across all 60+40 contexts. Relations are e.g. a0[0]^W0[0]^1 (C0c bit0=1), W0[0]^e0[0], a0[1]^W0[0]^W0[1] (C0c bit1=1), and one round-1 relation using Maj(a0,a_{-1},a_{-2})[0]=1 since IV words a_{-1}=0x6a09e667 and a_{-2}=0xbb67ae85 both have bit0=1. Message-block nullity 72 vs ≥69 forced by W12..W15 being context-constant (60 distinct tuples spanning 129 columns). Scripts mi_gf2.py, mi_gf2b.py.
findings.effect_if_real: Rules out linear/affine structure as an attack surface on the recovered state.

findings.claim: The apparent per-bit biases in a2 and a3 (bits 25/29 reading p=0.443/0.562, |z|=26–28 pooled) are NOT structure — they are a corollary of the forced Maj condition combined with only 60 sampled v values. Worth flagging because pooling contexts makes them look like a 26σ discovery.
findings.evidence: The Maj condition forbids (a2_i,a3_i)=(v_i,~v_i), so with the three survivors equiprobable, p(a2_i=1)=1/3 if v_i=1 else 2/3 (mirror for a3). Residuals against this prediction over all 1920 (context,bit) cells: a2 mean +0.00024, rms 0.01593 vs binomial sd 0.01613 (ratio 0.99); a3 mean +0.00054, rms 0.01625 (ratio 1.01) — a perfect fit. Predicted spread-inflation of pooled p across contexts = (1/6)/0.01710 = 9.74; measured 9.67 (a2) and 9.74 (a3). Context-level t-tests on the worst bit give t=−2.79 and +3.08, below the 4.1 Bonferroni threshold. Contrast W1/W2/W3 bit31, whose spread-inflation is 0.92 and t=60 — a real universal bias. Scripts mi_anom.py, mi_power.py.
findings.effect_if_real: Prevents a false 26σ 'per-bit bias' claim; also establishes that a2 determines a3 on 1/3 of bit positions (H(a3|a2,v)=21.33 bits), which is real but not exploitable since the table is indexed by the σ0-difference, not by a3.

findings.claim: (c) Per-bit entropy of every field and every message word is full to within 6e-4 bits, with the sole exceptions all traceable to the table: W1,W2,W3 (deficit 0.0587 bits each), and W10/W11 which inherit a fraction of it through the backward chain (0.0123 / 0.0190 bits). Nothing below 1 bit is unexplained.
findings.evidence: R19/R20 per-bit entropy sums: a0,W0,W4,e0,e1,e2,e3 all 31.9995–31.9997 (deficit 3e-4..5e-4, at the n-limited floor); c3 31.99968; a2/a3 31.958–31.961 (fully explained by the v-dependent 1/3–2/3 marginals above). Message words over 38,316 verified blocks: W0,W4..W9 all 31.999x with p(bit31)=0.497–0.506; W1,W2,W3 = 31.9394–31.9407 with p(bit31)=0.6238/0.6238/0.6245; W10 31.9877, W11 31.9810 (p(bit31)=0.5201); W12..W15 take only 60 distinct values (constant per context, forced). Script mi_fields.
findings.effect_if_real: Rules out per-bit message-word bias as an attack surface; confines all detectable non-uniformity in the corpus to the single known table mechanism.

detection_power: Sample sizes 51,268 (R19, 60 contexts) and 68,680 → 68,152 after deduplicating repeated (ctx,a0) draws (R20, 40 contexts, ~1704/context). All c3 results are on deduplicated data; all tests are Bonferroni-corrected for the number run and validated against a matched uniform-random control and/or shuffle nulls. THRESHOLDS: (1) Per-bit probability: sd(p)=0.00191 (R20), so |p−0.5|>0.0076 detectable at 4σ; observed max |z|=1.79 over 32 bits. (2) Mutual information, 2x2 tables: null E[MI]=1.05e-5 bits, 99.99%ile 1.59e-4 bits; 15,360 bit-bit tests run, max observed 1.6e-4 — exactly at the floor, nothing above it. (3) Linear/GF(2): corr sd = 0.00383; 17,280,000 (a0-mask, c3-mask) approximations tested, best 5.49σ vs 5.77σ expected as the max of that many noise gaussians, so any linear predictor has bias < 0.0092, removing < 2.4e-4 bits. (4) Additive-DFT, the matched filter for a modular residual: EXHAUSTIVE over every frequency of the low-16-bit and high-16-bit subgroups (131,070 frequencies) plus 4,000 random ones, per context, T(β)~Gamma(40,1). c3 max z = +5.23; uniform control max z = +5.58 — statistically identical. A CONCENTRATED deficit at any single frequency above 6.0e-4 bits would have shown at 4.5σ. (5) BROADLY-SPREAD deficit, via within-context collision counting (the aggregate of the DFT over a subgroup), 4σ upper limits: low 8 bits ≤ 0.0061 bits (observed +0.0011), low 16 bits ≤ 0.096 bits (observed −0.0057), low 20 bits ≤ 0.39 bits (observed −0.148). LIMITS OF THIS POWER, stated honestly: with ~68k samples I cannot see an entropy deficit spread thinly over the full 2^32 frequency space below roughly 0.006 bits (the low-byte limit, my tightest aggregate bound), and I cannot see any effect confined to a 2^-32-scale set — which is precisely the regime a real 20-round speedup would have to live in if it were not visible as a bias. That residual gap is why the convolution argument matters: it bounds the lever analytically (≤9.1e-4 bits from any table policy) rather than only statistically. Two structural caveats: only 60/40 distinct contexts exist, so per-context effects are tested with 40 degrees of freedom, and rows within a context share a0-determined dependence — I therefore used context-level t-tests and per-context grouped statistics wherever a pooled statistic could be confounded, which is exactly what exposed the a2/a3 bit-25/29 artifact. Scripts and logs are in /tmp/claude-1000/-home-administrator-sha/bc6b4995-3384-44e4-9203-a490e2389533/scratchpad/mi/ with prefix mi_ (mi_a_joint, mi_b_c3, mi_dft, mi_conv, mi_power, mi_dedup, mi_anom, mi_gf2, mi_gf2b, mi_lin, mi_fields, mi_final).

findings.claim: The three table lookups depend on the context ONLY through (KC0,KC1,KC2); v=a4=a5 enters ONLY the final Maj filter. Consequently a stage-3 survivor is a preimage for EXACTLY 2^k of the 2^32 values of v, where k=#{i: a2_i=a3_i}. If v could be chosen after the sweep, yield rises by 1/E[2^(k-32)] = 2^13.28. The obstruction is one specific inversion: (v,a6,a7,a10) -> (KC0,KC1,KC2) is a square map with no exploitable structure found (brute force 2^96).
findings.effect_if_real: Removes the entire (3/4)^32 = 2^-13.3 filter cost at R=19 and R=20, IF the inversion (a6,a7,a10) -> prescribed (KC0,KC1,KC2) at prescribed v can be solved for less than the attack's current cost. Counting says ~one context exists per desired (KC-triple, v); none was exhibited.
findings.evidence: relx_06: constructed two chain objects sharing (KC0,KC1,KC2) but with v differing by 0xDEADBEEF; the stage-3 survivor index set and every (a0,a1,a2,a3) quadruple were bit-identical (True/True), while Maj hits differed (9 vs 3). relx_09 part (d): over 533,539 stage-3 survivors, mean k=16.003, max k=28, min k>=2 observed; E[2^(k-32)] = 1.005884e-04 vs (3/4)^32 = 1.004524e-04; fraction with k>=1 is 100.0000%, giving prize = 9.942e3 = 2^13.28. relx_09 part 2: v-dependence NOT separable (8/8 distinct difference triples), a10-dependence NOT separable (8/8), a10->KC0 injective on [0,2^12) (4096/4096 distinct) but non-affine (4053 distinct consecutive differences).

findings.claim: The R=20 fourth-constraint residual c3 is a flat 2^-32 filter. No per-bit bias, no low/high-16-bit non-uniformity, no concentrated character, no dependence on a0, on the context, or on the Maj-filter statistic k.
findings.effect_if_real: No speedup available from steering c3; the 2^32 cost at R=20 stands. Rules out brief items (i)(a), (i)(b) and the table-policy part of (i)(c) at the stated resolution.
findings.evidence: relx_11 on 59,764,994 stage-3 survivors (870x the 68,680-row corpus): per-bit |p-1/2| < 1.94e-04 at 3 sigma, max|z|=2.12, chi2 23.7/32 df p=0.854; low-16-bit chi2 = 65535/65535 df (p=0.499), top-16-bit chi2 = 65366/65535 df (p=0.679); max |characteristic function| = 4.29e-04 vs null E[max] 4.31e-04, zero frequencies above 1.5x null over 2^16 frequencies. Independence c3 _|_ k: chi2 1414.0 on 1386 df (p=0.294), MI = 1.71e-05 bits vs chance level 1.67e-05 -- so the bound transfers from stage-3 survivors to the Maj-passing population. relx_03 on the corpus: MI(a0 low4; c3 low4) = 0.00211 vs chance 0.00236; MI(a0 high4; c3 low4) = 0.00269 vs chance 0.00236; per-context chi2(low 8 bits) p-values uniform (mean 0.420, 5 of 40 below 0.05).

findings.claim: The (3/4)^32 Maj filter is exactly (3/4)^32 and is NOT steerable by the table's representative policy. a2 and a3 are uncorrelated bitwise to 2.6e-5.
findings.effect_if_real: Rules out brief item (iii) 'the (3/4)^32 filter could be improved' by any per-bit bias mechanism, and the representative-policy half of item (i)(c).
findings.evidence: relx_07 (max table, 24 ctx x 2^24 a0, 102,450,763 stage-3 survivors): E[2^k]/(3/2)^32 = 1.00110, bootstrap 99% CI [0.9998, 1.0024]; k-histogram vs Binomial(32,1/2) chi2 = 33.2 on 28 df (p=0.228); per-bit P(a2_i=a3_i)-1/2 bounded by 2.62e-05 for a uniform shift, giving yield factor within [0.99944, 1.00056]. relx_07 (MIN-representative table, 16 ctx x 2^23): ratio 1.00098, 99% CI [0.9987, 1.0034]. relx_05 (40 ctx x 2^23, 85,372,917 survivors): q_i = P(a2_i=v_i AND a3_i!=v_i) equals 1/4 with max|z|=1.77 over 32 bits; prod(1-q_i)/(3/4)^32 = 0.99975, 3-sigma band [0.9938, 1.0058]; observed pass rate ratio 0.9955 +-3.2%.

findings.claim: No context is systematically better than another, and contexts sharing v share no structure at all -- the K_seeds independence assumption holds.
findings.effect_if_real: Rules out brief item (i)(b) and lens item (c). Confirms the current cost accounting over multiple context seeds.
findings.evidence: relx_05: 40 contexts x 2^23, hits/ctx mean 213.4 var 187.8, dispersion chi2 = 34.3 on 39 df (p=0.683), bounding context-to-context relative yield sd below ~5.6% at 3 sigma; corr(popcount(v), hits) = +0.113 with sd 0.158. relx_09 part 1: same target, same v, 6 different (a6,a7,a10), same 2^21 contiguous a0 range -- all 15 pairwise stage-3 survivor-set overlaps within ratio [0.9974, 1.0028] of the independence baseline (|intersection| ~135,000 vs baseline ~135,700).

findings.claim: No near-collision or neighbour structure among preimages: survival of adjacent a0 is uncorrelated at every lookup stage, and within-context a0 XOR-distance matches the binomial baseline exactly.
findings.effect_if_real: Rules out lens item (a) and any 'skip the lookups by predicting survival from a0' shortcut.
findings.evidence: relx_04 (contiguous 2^22 sweep, stage rates 0.6337/0.4017/0.2545 matching the documented 0.634/0.402/0.254): additive-lag autocovariance of survival at lags 1..64 max|z| = 3.00 (s1), 2.16 (s2), 2.20 (s3), 0.05 (final); XOR-neighbour correlation over all 22 swept bits max|z| = 4.08 (s1), 3.11 (s2), 3.27 (s3) -- 1 of ~320 tests above |z|=4, as expected by chance. relx_02 corpus: r19 within-context 21,899,269 pairs, observed/expected at Hamming d=1..6 = 0.00/0.40/1.23/1.00/0.93/1.01; r20 58,965,211 pairs = 0.00/1.32/1.00/1.01/0.99/1.00; min distance 2 against explicit extreme-value baseline P(min<=2)=0.9326 (r19), 0.9993 (r20). The d=0 entries (206, 530) are the corpus RNG resampling identical a0, confirmed by a random-subsample control.

findings.claim: The chain a0 -> (a1,a2,a3) is injective at the birthday rate; there is no hidden many-to-one collapse that would change the yield accounting.
findings.effect_if_real: Rules out lens item (b). The single corpus a2-collision with distinct a0 was chance.
findings.evidence: 3 contexts x 2^24 contiguous sweep, 12,806,245 stage-3 survivors: within-context value collisions observed/birthday-expected = 0.993 (a1, z=-0.56), 0.979 (a2, z=-1.71), 0.999 (a3, z=-0.06), against 6364 expected pairs each; a0 is the control at 0 (swept contiguously). W3 sits at 1.572x = 1/0.634, exactly the forced max-representative image density.

findings.claim: Two apparent per-bit anomalies in the message words (W10 bit 11 at naive z=+11, W11 bit 21 at naive z=-15) are artifacts of treating 38,316 blocks from only 60 contexts as independent. Within every context W0=a0+c, W9=c-a1, W10=c-a2, W11=c-a3 hold EXACTLY, so those words inherit a2/a3's forced v-dependent 1/3-2/3 law.
findings.effect_if_real: No finding; a false positive I generated and then killed. Recorded because the project has previously been burned by exactly this kind of mis-specified baseline.
findings.evidence: relx_13: the identities hold 60/60 contexts for each of W0(-a0), W9(+a1), W10(+a2), W11(+a3). Recomputing the per-bit test from the 60 context-level means instead of 38,316 block-level samples gives max|z| = 2.13 (W10 bit 11) and 2.89 (W11 bit 21), with between-context sd of p equal to 0.102 and 0.101. The W1/W2/W3 bit-31 bias (p=0.6238, clustered z=51) is the known max-representative bias and survives clustering. The 111 'repeated 32-bit words' per column are 111 identical FULL 16-word blocks (the corpus drew a0 with replacement), not word-level structure. Within-context block distance deficit (190.45 vs 191.88 cross-context on 384 bits) is fully accounted for by W10 and W11 alone (15.31, 15.27 vs 16.00).

findings.claim: Exact identity a_{j+1} = sigma0(W_{j+1}) + W_j - KC_j for j=0,1,2, which removes G, F12, F23 from the description entirely. The R=20 fourth constraint c3 = sigma0(W4) + W3 - K3p has the SAME shape -- it is one more copy of the same equation with no free state word to absorb it.
findings.effect_if_real: A cleaner statement of the attack (find a chain W0->W1->W2->W3 of stored roots with prescribed offsets) and a precise statement of why R=20 costs 2^32. Not itself a speedup.
findings.evidence: relx_08: reconstructing W2 from a3 = s0(W3)+W2-KC2 and then W1 from a2 = s0(W2)+W1-KC1 yields stored table roots for 100.0000% of 66,928 (R=19) and 66,983 (R=20) stage-3 survivors. Follows from the table's defining property s0(W)-W = I.

findings.claim: Root multiplicity of u -> sigma0(u)-u quantified exactly: enumerating all roots instead of the single stored representative multiplies candidates per swept a0 by 3.67 = 2^1.87.
findings.effect_if_real: Quantifies the brief's 'about a quarter of the available solutions'. Known, not new, but the exact multiplier is 3.67 and the achievable yield is 0.93 candidates per swept a0 rather than 0.2545.
findings.evidence: relx_14, 2^23 random indices across the max/min/root2/root3 tables: P(>=1 root)=0.633539, P(>=2)=0.263906, P(>=3)=0.079453; mean >=1.542 roots per non-empty fibre vs the random-map value 1/(1-1/e)=1.582; max and min tables agree exactly on which indices are hit; all stored entries verified as genuine roots.

headline: Every candidate lever in the brief is a sharp negative (c3 flat to 1.9e-4 per bit on 59.8M samples; the (3/4)^32 filter exact to 0.24% and unmoved by the table policy; no context better than another; no a0 near-neighbour structure; chain injective at birthday rate). The one real finding is structural: the three lookups depend on the context ONLY through (KC0,KC1,KC2) while v enters ONLY the Maj filter, which makes each stage-3 survivor a preimage for exactly 2^k of the 2^32 values of v -- a 2^13.3 speedup that is blocked by a single well-defined 2^96 inversion.
detection_power: Thresholds, all stated at 3 sigma unless noted, with Bonferroni correction over the number of tests run. (1) c3 per-bit bias: n = 59,764,994 (all stage-3 survivors at R=20, 14 contexts x 2^24 swept a0), sd 6.47e-05, so |p-1/2| < 1.94e-04 -- 30x tighter than the 5.7e-03 the 68,680-row corpus alone allows; 32 tests, Bonferroni |z|>3.2, max observed 2.12. (2) c3 concentrated bias: characteristic function computed at 2^16 low and 2^16 top frequencies; max |phi(t)| = 4.29e-04 against null E[max] = sqrt(ln N / n) = 4.31e-04. NOTE the limit: a bias spread thinly over many of the 2^32 characters is invisible at any n we can reach -- this test excludes only the concentrated kind, which is the kind that would make P(c3=0) exceed 2^-32 by a detectable factor. (3) Transfer of that bound to the Maj-passing population rests on c3 _|_ k: MI = 1.71e-05 bits vs chance level 1.67e-05, chi2 1414.0/1386 df. (4) Maj filter exactness: E[2^k]/(3/2)^32 = 1.00110 with bootstrap 99% CI [0.9998, 1.0024] on 102,450,763 survivors; the estimator is tail-dominated (bins k>=20 carry 75.8% of E[2^k] and hold 11,033,493 samples, so the tail is well sampled). Two independent runs (max and min tables) both give +0.10%, i.e. ~+2.5 sigma combined -- I treat this as consistent with 1 and in any case worth at most a 0.1% speedup. (5) Per-bit a2/a3 agreement: sd 4.94e-05, bounding a uniform per-bit excess |d| < 2.62e-05, i.e. yield factor within [0.99944, 1.00056]; a d of 0.01 would have shown as a 1.24x factor. (6) Context yield heterogeneity: 40 contexts, mean 213.4 hits each, dispersion chi2 34.3/39 df; bounds context-to-context relative yield sd below ~5.6%. Detecting a 2x-better context class would have been trivial. (7) a0 neighbour survival: ~320 tests (64 additive lags x 4 stages + 22 bit-flips x 3 stages) at n = 2^22 per context, max |z| = 4.08 -- one exceedance expected by chance. Power here is high for stage-1/2/3 survival (rates 0.63/0.40/0.25) and essentially nil for the final 2.5e-05 rate, which I state rather than gloss. (8) Corpus XOR-distance: 21.9M (r19) and 59.0M (r20) within-context pairs; ratios to the C(32,d)/2^32 baseline are within 1% at d=4,5,6, but expected counts at d=1 are only 0.16 and 0.44, so a <20x enhancement at d=1 would not have been visible from the corpus -- which is exactly why I ran the contiguous sweep in (7). (9) Cross-context overlap: resolution 0.3% on the survivor-set overlap ratio. (10) Injectivity: 6364 expected birthday pairs per statistic on 12.8M survivors, so a 3% excess would have shown. Mutual-information floor throughout ~1.7e-05 bits, below the brief's 1e-04 bar. Principal caveats: the 59.8M-sample c3 bound is measured on stage-3 survivors rather than Maj-passers and transfers only via the independence test in (3); and the compensating context needed for the 2^13.3 lever is argued to exist by a counting argument on a square 4-word map, not exhibited.

headline: Sharp negative on a route past 20 rounds: on 214,583 freshly generated 21-round candidates the fourth and fifth constraint residuals (C3 at W19, C4 at W20) are uniform and mutually independent to the limit of ~2x10^5 samples, so 21 rounds costs the full 2^64 above 19; an exhaustive symbolic search over 1,485 legal context families confirms the Sigma0 barrier is unremovable — the only quantified lever found is the already-known single-root table policy, worth exactly 1/0.63381^3 = 2^1.974.

findings.claim: C3 and C4 are independent: the fifth constraint's residual carries no usable information about the fourth. 21 rounds therefore costs 2^64 above 19 (2^79.26 swept a0), with no shortcut.
findings.evidence: Regenerated an R=21 corpus keeping the context: 214,583 candidates (212,083 distinct a0) from 84 fresh 21-round targets over 8.4e9 swept a0, using make_context extended to a4..a12 and the on-disk sigma0(u)-u table (/tmp/.../scratchpad/lens5/L5_10_gen.py, big21.npz). Formulas validated two ways: against the reference forward pass on 400 random messages (W4, W5, e4, C3, C4 all exact, L5_11_validate.py), and end-to-end on real candidates by rebuilding the 16-word block and expanding the schedule -- C0=C1=C2=0 and the stored c3, c4 equal W19-W19_true and the W20 residual for 25/25 (L5_12_e2e.py). Tests (L5_60_c3c4.py): 1024 GF(2) bit-pair correlations C3_i x C4_j, max |z| = 3.62 (Bonferroni 5% needs 4.06; expected max of 1024 |N(0,1)| is 3.4); top singular value of the z-matrix 11.18 against a null of 2*sqrt(32)=11.3; joint independence chi-square on low-4 bits z=+0.07, low-6 bits z=-1.48; shuffle-controlled mutual information excess -0.0004 (k=6) and +0.019 (k=8, within the estimator's own noise).
findings.effect_if_real: None. Had a correlation of even 1 bit existed, R=21 would drop from 2^79.26 to 2^78.26; nothing of the sort is present.

findings.claim: The fourth-constraint residual is flat: no region of it can be steered onto by choosing the context, and no local search around a near-miss is possible. At most 0.46 bits could ever be gained this way.
findings.evidence: Pooled C3 and C4 over 212,083 distinct-a0 R=21 candidates: 8 exact collisions against a uniform expectation of 10.47, giving a 95% Poisson upper limit of 14.4, i.e. collision-probability elevation <= 1.38x and Renyi-2 entropy >= 31.54 bits (L5_61_pred.py). Per-bit means max |z| 2.92 (C3) and 2.11 (C4) over 64 tests. Low-k marginals of C3 in the supplied corpus_r20, pooled per context (exact, since subtracting K3p is a cyclic shift on the low k bits and chi-square is shift invariant): z = +0.48, +0.72, +2.38, +2.13 for k = 6, 8, 10, 12 after removing 528 duplicate-a0 rows (L5_22_c3dedup.py). Separately, because sigma0 is GF(2)-bijective, C3=0 is exactly W4 = sigma0^-1(K3p - W3); the difference residual d3 = W4 - sigma0^-1(K3p-W3) and its C4 analogue d4 are also flat -- mean Hamming weight 15.998 +- 0.006 against 16, zero rows with weight <= 3, minimum |d3| = 6091 over 212k rows (L5_64_sigmainv.py). NOTE on an artifact: the supplied corpus_r20 shows 531 raw C3 'collisions' against 0.55 expected; all 530 within-context ones are the same (ctx,a0) drawn twice by the random sweep (~6.7e7 draws per context gives ~13 repeats each) and vanish on dedup.
findings.effect_if_real: A concentrated residual would let one screen contexts so K3p lands on a heavy value; the collision bound caps that at 0.46 bits, and a local search on W4 is excluded outright.

findings.claim: The residual is not predictable from anything available before the three table lookups -- not from a0, not from the context words, not from where the candidate sits inside the 3^32 submask set -- and no context is systematically more productive than another.
findings.evidence: On 212,083 R=21 candidates (L5_61_pred.py, L5_62_subfam.py, L5_63_big20.py): GF(2) correlations of every C3/C4 bit with every bit of a0, W0 and e0 -- max |z| 3.65 over 6144 tests, Bonferroni threshold 4.06, single-correlation detection floor 0.0088; top singular values 10.4-11.4 against an 11.3 null. Shuffle-controlled MI between each byte of a0 and the low byte of C3/C4: |excess| <= 0.0025 bits. Proxy hit event C3 = 0 mod 2^8 (864 hits, expected 828): chi-square across 84 contexts z=-0.62, across 13 popcount(a3^v) groups z=+0.32, across the high byte of a0 z=+0.03; same pattern for C4 and for mod 2^12. Correlations of the per-context mean of each C3 bit with the bits of the context words a4(=v), a6, a7, a10, a11 and of K3p, over 60 R=20 contexts: max |z| 3.53 over 6144 tests. Per-context candidate yield pooled over 4 corpora (244 contexts, 1.44e10 + swept a0): chi-square 272.3 on 240 dof, z=+1.47, bounding any extra-Poisson spread in per-context yield to under ~1%.
findings.effect_if_real: A predictor from a0 or the context would be a direct speedup by its conditional-entropy reduction; none exists above the stated floors. Context screening is worth at most ~0.02 bits.

findings.claim: The (3/4)^32 submask filter cannot be sharpened: its density on the a2,a3 the lookups actually produce is exactly (3/4)^32, the three lookups are mutually independent, and a2,a3 are uniform on the 3^32 set. Nor does widening the accepted eps set help.
findings.evidence: Dedicated per-stage counter over 4.8e9 swept a0, 16 R=20 targets (L5_70_rates.py, rates.log): P(lookup1 hit) = 0.6336601 +- 7e-6, P(lookup2 | 1) = 0.6336764 +- 9e-6, P(lookup3 | 2) = 0.6336671 +- 1.1e-5 -- identical, so the lookups are independent; P(eps==0 | solution) = 1.006468e-4 +- 2.9e-7, i.e. 1.00193 +- 0.00286 times (3/4)^32 = 1.004524e-4 (z=+0.68). Pooled candidate density over big20+big21 (1.44e10 swept a0) is 2.553931e-5 against the model 0.63381^3*(3/4)^32 = 2.557630e-5, ratio 0.99855 +- 0.00165. Uniformity of the surviving pair on the 3^32 support (L5_30_r19.py, L5_33_corr.py, 51,063 distinct R=19 preimages): P(a2_i != v_i) = 0.6660 and P(a3_i != v_i) = 0.3327 against 2/3 and 1/3, max |z| 1.99 over 64 tests; popcount(a3^v) versus Binomial(32,1/3) chi-square z=+0.30, mean 10.646 against 10.667; properly centred within-context bit-pair correlations of a3^v and a2^v all <= 0.014 (max z 3.2 over 496 tests). Widening the filter is also provably a loss: eps = Q - P with P, Q disjoint submasks, so P(eps=0) = (3/4)^32 is the mode and each single-bit value has only (3/4)^31/8 = 1/6 of it, so admitting the 32 single-bit values multiplies yield by 6.3 at 33x the lookup cost.
findings.effect_if_real: Confirms the filter is already at its optimum for a single provisional value; there is no better sub-family and no better provisional eps.

findings.claim: No context family clears the Sigma0 barrier. Over an exhaustive symbolic search of 1,485 realizable context families, the fourth constraint is never solvable for a1, a2 or a3; promoting a4 leaves the a4->C0 edge heavy in all 156 families, and promoting a5 leaves a5->C1 heavy in all 108. Every free context word also touches C0 and C1, so none can be re-chosen after the fact to satisfy C3.
findings.evidence: Built a canonical sum-of-atoms symbolic algebra for the R=21 compression function with Maj/Ch simplification on structural equality and on saturating constants (the family's two levers), plus an occurrence classifier that separates 'absent', 'linear', 'inside one sigma0 of a linear form' (solvable by the sigma0(u)-u table) from 'heavy' (L5_50_symdep.py). Enumerated promote-sets over {a4,a5,a6} x all equality patterns on the remaining a4..a7 x all saturations e8..e11 in {0, 0xFFFFFFFF, free}: 2,835 configurations, 1,485 with realizable saturations (a saturation is rejected when the a_r it needs would depend on an unknown). Control reproduces the published attack exactly -- (C0,a1), (C1,a2), (C2,a3) solvable and (C1,a3) absent, the family's Consequence 1. Results: (C3, x) solvable only for a promoted a4 (156), a5 (21) or a6 (6), never for a1/a2/a3; (C0,a4) = heavy in 156/156; (C1,a5) = heavy in 108/108. The best configuration found -- promote a5, a6=a7=a4, e8=-1, e10=-1, e11=0 -- makes all five constraints have a solvable entry but only by closing a cycle (C0 needs a5, C3/C4 need a1..a3) and it destroys the family's (C1,a3)='absent' property, trading one 2^32 for another. Reach table: every free word a4..a12 occurs in C0 and C1. Numerically confirmed on random instances (L5_53_numdep.py): the (C1,a3) 'absent' entry reproduces exactly, and the deferral probabilities are P(C0 unchanged when a2,a3 leave the provisional 0) = 219/2,097,152 = 1.044e-4, matching (3/4)^32, against 0/2,097,152 (< 5e-7, i.e. at least 210x worse) for a4 in C0 and for a5 in C0 and C1.
findings.effect_if_real: Confirms the project's claim that the barrier is a dependency cycle through Sigma0 of an unknown, and that it survives the whole space of saturation/equality context conditions -- not just the ones tried by hand.

findings.claim: sigma0, sigma1, Sigma0 and Sigma1 are all GF(2)-bijective, which closes the 'image coset' idea and shows the barrier is purely the cycle, not the invertibility: if the cycle could be broken, C3 would be solvable with probability 1, not 0.634.
findings.evidence: GF(2) rank of each 32x32 matrix is 32 (computed from the images of the basis vectors); the sigma0 inverse was built and verified on 10,000 random words (L5_64_sigmainv.py). Consequence: C3=0 is exactly W4 = sigma0^-1(K3p - W3) and C4=0 is W5 = sigma0^-1(K4p - W4) -- two exact functional determinations, not partial conditions. There is therefore no linear condition on W3 alone that C3=0 implies, so no table-policy trick can pre-satisfy part of C3.
findings.effect_if_real: Rules out a whole class of would-be levers (biasing the stored representative into a coset of Im(sigma0)); the 0.634 lookup hit rate is a property of u -> sigma0(u)-u, not of sigma0.

findings.claim: The 19-round preimage set carries no structure beyond what the construction forces: the only exact GF(2) affine relations are seven carry-free consequences of W0 = a0 + const and its siblings, and the only message-word bit biases are W1, W2, W3 matching the table's maximal-representative distribution exactly.
findings.evidence: GF(2) rank of the 51,063 x 449 bit matrix over {a0..a3, W0..W4, e0..e3, v} plus an affine 1 is 442, deficiency exactly 7; the seven null vectors were extracted and are all low-bit identities such as 0 = a0[0]^W0[0]^1 and 0 = W0[0]^e0[0] (L5_31_null.py). These are forced: C0c = 0x03f777b3 and Ce0 = 0x9cbf5a55 are fixed by the IV alone, and W0-a0 == C0c, e0-a0 == Ce0 on every row. Message words (L5_32_msg.py): treating the 60 contexts as the sampling unit (rows inside a context share W12..W15 and are all functions of one swept a0, so the naive z-scores of 45-59 on W12..W15 are spurious), every word has cluster-robust max |z| <= 3.4 over 512 tests except W1, W2, W3, whose bit-31 means are 0.508 (|z| ~ 50). Compared against 4e6 random probes of the table itself, whose maximal representative has bit-31 mean 0.6224, bit-30 0.5614, bit-29 0.5309: the corpus W1/W2/W3 match that baseline with max |z| 2.5 over 96 tests in both corpora (L5_40_table.py).
findings.effect_if_real: Nothing to exploit; it also means the reachable set really is 'a quarter of the solutions, at random', as hypothesised.

findings.claim: Storing all roots of sigma0(u)-u instead of only the maximal one multiplies candidates per swept a0 by exactly 1/0.63381^3 = 3.9276 = 2^1.974, at every round count. This is the 'quarter of the solutions' already on the known list, now given its exact value; the root2 and root3 tables already exist on disk.
findings.evidence: Each u is the root of exactly one value of sigma0(u)-u, so the expected number of roots per table index is exactly 1.0, against the 0.63381 hit rate of the single-root table; measured multiplicity over 4e6 random indices using sigma0_u_table.npy, sigma0_u_table_root2.npy and sigma0_u_table_root3_refuter1.npy is 0 roots 0.3662, 1 root 0.3697, 2 roots 0.1847, >=3 roots 0.0794, mean 1.542 truncated at three against the exact 1/0.63381 = 1.5778 (L5_40_table.py). The three lookups were measured to be independent (hit rates 0.633660, 0.633676, 0.633667 over 4.8e9 swept a0), so the gain compounds as the cube. As a bonus it removes the only measured bias in the corpus (the bit-31 skew of W1, W2, W3).
findings.effect_if_real: R=20 goes from 2^47.26 to 2^45.28 swept a0 per preimage; R=19 from 2^15.26 to 2^13.28. Cost: ~3x table memory or a multi-root layout, and more divergent branching per swept a0.

findings.claim: The measured single-root cost of a 20-round preimage is 2^47.26 swept a0, 1.86 bits above the 2^45.4 quoted in the brief -- and the gap equals the 1.974-bit multi-root factor almost exactly. Either the quoted figure already assumes an all-roots table, or the GPU run counts swept a0 differently; worth reconciling before the number goes in a paper.
findings.evidence: Pooled candidate density (C0,C1,C2 and the submask condition all satisfied) is 2.553931e-5 +- 0.17% over 1.44e10 swept a0 across 144 fresh contexts, i.e. 39,155 swept a0 = 2^15.257 per 19-round preimage -- which reproduces the paper's own 2^15.26 exactly. C3 is a flat 2^-32 filter (established above), so R=20 = 2^47.257 and R=21 = 2^79.257 under the same accounting. With the multi-root gain applied, R=20 = 2^45.283, which is the quoted 2^45.4 to within rounding.
findings.effect_if_real: If the published R=20 figure is the idealised multi-root one while the implementation is single-root, the honest single-target cost is 3.9x higher than stated; if instead the GPU already exploits multiple roots, that should be said explicitly.

detection_power: Sample sizes: 214,583 R=21 candidates (212,083 distinct a0) from 84 targets over 8.4e9 swept a0; 153,183 R=20 candidates from 60 targets over 6.0e9; plus the supplied 51,268 R=19 and 68,680 R=20 rows. A separate counting run covered 4.8e9 swept a0 and 1.22e9 triangular solutions. All analyses deduplicate on (ctx, a0): the random sweep repeats an a0 often enough that ~0.8% of rows are duplicates, and that artifact alone produced a spurious 967x 'collision excess' in C3 before it was removed. Thresholds at N = 212,083: one sigma on a bit-mean is 0.00109 (so a per-bit probability bias below 0.0033 at 3 sigma, 0.0044 after Bonferroni over 32 tests, is invisible); one sigma on a GF(2) bit-pair correlation is 0.00217, Bonferroni floor over 1024 tests 0.0088; shuffle-controlled byte-level mutual information is resolved to about 0.002 bits; the collision test bounds the residual's Renyi-2 entropy at >= 31.54 bits (elevation <= 1.38x). Every family of tests is reported with its own Bonferroni threshold and, for chi-squares, with (chi2-dof)/sqrt(2 dof). The largest single deviation anywhere in the study was a +2.85 sigma over-dispersion of per-context yield in big21, which fell to +1.47 when pooled with the other three corpora, i.e. noise. Three hard limitations. (1) A single heavy atom in the residual of weight up to about 2^-18 would be invisible to 3.7e5 samples and to the collision test, which sees only sum p^2; only a globally concentrated residual is excluded. (2) Not one C3=0 event was observed (0 in 3.7e5 candidates, expectation 1.6e-5 per corpus), so every independence claim is about the global joint law of (C3,C4), not about behaviour conditioned on the solution point -- a dependence that only manifests at (0,0) is not excluded by any amount of this kind of sampling. (3) The symbolic search covers promote-sets within {a4,a5,a6}, all equality patterns on a4..a7 and saturations of e8..e11 to 0 or 0xFFFFFFFF; it does not cover conditions that tie a context word to an unknown, multi-block message freedom, or bitwise (as opposed to word-level) context conditions other than the submask pattern already in use. Scripts and logs are in /tmp/claude-1000/-home-administrator-sha/bc6b4995-3384-44e4-9203-a490e2389533/scratchpad/lens5/ with the L5_ prefix (generators L5_10_gen.py and L5_70_rates.py, validators L5_11_validate.py and L5_12_e2e.py, analyses L5_20 through L5_64, symbolic search L5_50/L5_51/L5_53); the regenerated corpora are big21.npz and big20.npz in the same directory.

headline: No linear or affine lever exists: the GF(2) rank deficit of the preimage set is fully accounted for by the construction (three carry-free LSB relations per context and nothing else), the fourth-constraint residual is uniform and independent of a0, of the context, and of the max-representative bias in W3 down to a per-context correlation of 0.0033, and at R=21 the fifth constraint c4 = s0(W5)+W4-K4p is independent of c3 to MI < 1e-5 bits. The only genuine unexplained structure is in the sigma0 table itself: the exact image of sigma0(u)-u is 0.633672724 of 2^32 (not 1-1/e), its hit rate varies with the index residue class at z=311, and one index (0x20000000) is lost to a sentinel collision. All three are too small to be levers.

findings.claim: Within a context the 19-round preimage blocks span an affine subspace of GF(2)^512 of dimension exactly 381, and the entire 131-bit deficit is forced: 128 from the shared W12..W15 plus exactly 3 relations, which are the carry-free LSBs of the three table equations. Identical in all 60 contexts. No hidden subspace.
findings.evidence: lin_A_rank.py / lin_C_null2.py on corpus_r19['messages'] (38,316 blocks, 60 contexts, 630-640 per context). Exact GF(2) elimination on the difference matrix, not a statistical test. Per-context rank = 381 for all 60 contexts; nullspace of W0..W11 has dim exactly 3 in every context and is spanned by the same three vectors: W0[0]^W1[3,7,18]^W9[0], W1[0]^W2[3,7,18]^W10[0], W2[0]^W3[3,7,18]^W11[0] (bits 3,7,18 are precisely the support of sigma0(x)[0], so these are bit 0 of the three modular lookup equations). Global rank over all 38,315 differences = 440 = 512 - 69 - 3, where 69 = 128 - 59 is the artifact of only 60 distinct (W12..W15) values.
findings.effect_if_real: None. A rank materially below min(n-1,512) would have meant the reachable message set is a small subspace; it is not.

findings.claim: The fourth-constraint residual c3 is uniform and carries no linear information about a0. Over 3.2M lookup-survivors, 2224 mask pairs (alpha.a0 XOR beta.c3) give zero exceedances at a per-context detection floor of |corr| = 0.0033 (bias 0.0016 in probability); c3 is chi-square-uniform on 2^16 low and 2^16 high bins with |z| <= 1.4.
findings.evidence: lin_K_seq.py (contiguous a0 sweep, 6 R=20 contexts x 2^21 a0, 3,202,878 rows surviving the three lookups) + lin_L_ana.py. Section B: 1200 random + 1024 single-bit mask pairs, chi2_6 max = 24.9 vs Bonferroni threshold 40.0, mean 6.29 (expected 6). Section A: k=4,8,12,14,16 low and high, all |z| <= 2.2. Independently on corpus_r20 (68,680 rows, 40 contexts): 20,000 random mask pairs, chi2_40 max = 89.3 vs threshold 107.0, 0 exceedances; 32x32 single-bit matrix max chi2_40 = 80.4 vs threshold 97.7, 0 exceedances; 10,512 Fourier frequencies, max |E e^{2pi i f c3/2^32}| = 0.0125 vs expected max 0.0116.
findings.effect_if_real: A predictor of any c3 bit from a0 before the three lookups would be a direct 2^k speedup at R=20. None exists at this power.

findings.claim: c3 has no locality in a0 either: c3 at a0 and at a0+delta are bit-uncorrelated for delta in {1,2,3,4,8,64,1024}, and Maj-filter survivors are Poisson-spaced along a0. Sweeping a0 sequentially neither wastes nor gains work.
findings.evidence: lin_L_ana.py sections C and D on the contiguous sweep. ~136,000 matched (a0, a0+delta) pairs per delta per context, 3 contexts; max |z| on 32-bit agreement rates = 3.9 against a Bonferroni threshold of 3.8 for 672 tests (i.e. nothing). Survivor gaps: mean 60084 sd 62460; mean 38087 sd 32228; mean 41782 sd 40723 — sd ~ mean, the Poisson signature.
findings.effect_if_real: Clustering of survivors, or a slowly-varying c3, would have allowed skipping regions of the a0 sweep.

findings.claim: The strong max-representative bias in W3 is completely destroyed in c3, so no choice of table representative policy can move the fourth-constraint distribution. Modular concentration |E e^{2pi i W3/2^32}| = 0.154 collapses to 0.0039 (pure noise) in c3 — attenuation of 40x.
findings.evidence: lin_E_cmp.py / lin_G_c3.py on corpus_r20 (N=68,680). W3 f=1 Fourier coefficient 0.15415, matching the table-sampled max-representative baseline 0.15803; s0(W4) gives 0.00402; W3+s0(W4) gives 0.00174; c3 gives 0.00393 against a noise floor of 1/sqrt(N) = 0.00382. Per-context |c(c3)| mean 0.0232 vs noise expectation 0.0214. Because s0 is a bijection and W4 is effectively uniform, every Fourier mode of c3 is the product of a ~0 factor with whatever W3 contributes.
findings.effect_if_real: This kills value-type (c): rebuilding the 16 GB table with a min/median/random representative policy cannot help at R=20.

findings.claim: At R=21 the fifth constraint is c4 = s0(W5) + W4 - K4p with K4p = W20 - s1(W18) - W13, and it is statistically independent of c3: mutual information <= 9.5e-6 bits at 16x16 bins and max |corr(alpha.c3 XOR beta.c4)| = 0.00081 over 632 mask pairs. R=21 therefore costs a full 2^64 on top of the R=20 structure, with no discount from correlated residuals.
findings.evidence: lin_O_r21.py (derivation validated exactly against the reference implementation: for random 16-word messages, s0(W5)+W4-K4p == 0 and s0(W4)+W3-K3p == 0 identically), then 8 R=21 contexts x 2^23 contiguous a0 = 17,078,664 rows surviving the three lookups, 1751 Maj-survivors. lin_P_r21ana.py: joint chi2 at k=4,6,8,10 in low/low, high/high, low/high pairings, all |z| <= 1.96; MI bounds 9.5e-6 (k=4), 1.7e-4 (k=6), 2.7e-3 (k=8) bits. Mask search max |corr| 0.00081 vs expected max 0.00061 at N=1.7e7. On Maj-survivors alone (n=1751) chi2 p = 0.38 and 0.30.
findings.effect_if_real: A dependence would have cut the R=21 cost below 2^64; there is none.

findings.claim: The (3/4)^32 Maj filter is exactly the maximum-entropy filter on 3^32: the three allowed (a3,a2) bit patterns occur with probability exactly 1/3 each, uniformly across all 32 bit positions and all contexts, and the overall survival rate is exactly (3/4)^32. There is no residual skew to sharpen the filter with.
findings.evidence: lin_F_maj.py: pooled over 2.2M bit-cells, P(allowed pattern) = 0.3333 +- 0.0008 with zero mass on forbidden patterns; per (context, bit) chi2_2 over 1920 (r19) and 1280 (r20) cells has mean 2.020 / 2.037 against an expectation of 2.0, with tail fraction 0.0010 / 0.0016 above the p=1e-3 point. lin_M_majrate.py: 40 fresh R=20 contexts x 2^23 contiguous a0 = 85,371,447 lookup-survivors yielding 8,569 Maj-survivors vs 8,576.5 expected; ratio 0.9991, z = -0.08 (resolution +-1.1% at 1 sigma).
findings.effect_if_real: Rules out improving the 13.281-bit loss by biasing toward favourable bit patterns — the attack already lands uniformly on 3^32.

findings.claim: Contexts are interchangeable: per-context 19- and 20-round yields are exactly Poisson, bounding the extra-Poisson relative sd of context quality at 0.015 (1 sigma). And c3's distribution does not depend on which context produced it.
findings.evidence: Yield dispersion on equal a0 budgets: r19 chi2 = 50.3 on 59 dof (p = 0.78), r20 chi2 = 44.0 on 39 dof (p = 0.27); implied extra-Poisson relative sd 0.0000 (r19) and 0.0086 (r20), 1-sigma upper bound 0.0035 / 0.0149. lin_H_mod.py context-dependence: chi2 of (ctx, c3 mod 2^k) and (ctx, top-k bits of c3) for k=1..7, all |z| <= 2.20 over 14 tests.
findings.effect_if_real: Kills value-type (b): screening contexts for a better residual distribution buys nothing.

findings.claim: The image of u -> sigma0(u)-u is exactly 2,721,603,628 of 2^32 = 0.633672724, not the random-map value 1-1/e = 0.632120559, and its root-multiplicity distribution is under-dispersed relative to Poisson(1). This is exact, from a full-domain computation, not an estimate.
findings.evidence: lin_Q_img.py, two independent full 2^32 computations: (a) marking arr[sigma0(u)-u]=1 for all u gives image = 2,721,603,628; (b) counting non-sentinel entries of the 16 GB table gives 2,721,603,627 (one fewer, see the sentinel finding). Multiplicities from the root2/root3 tables: P(>=1) = 0.633672724, P(>=2) = 0.264262270, P(>=3) = 0.079507635 against Poisson(1) values 0.632120559, 0.264241118, 0.080301397 — more singletons, thinner tail. Previously logged figures of 63.21%/26.44%/8.02% in multiroot_build.log came from stride-64 subsamples and understate the first-root coverage. Consequence: the exact three-lookup survival rate is 0.633672724^3 = 0.254446 (measured 0.2545 over 84M swept a0 in lin_K_seq_big.log), 0.74% above the random-map estimate, and exhausting all roots instead of only the max representative would give exactly 3.93011x more solutions per swept a0.
findings.effect_if_real: Pins the 'about a quarter' constant to 0.254446 and the all-roots gain to 3.93011x. The deviation from the random-map model is real but its own effect is only +0.74%.

findings.claim: The sigma0 table's hit rate is not constant across index residue classes: it varies with the low bits of the lookup index at overwhelming significance (chi2 = 7278 on 255 dof at mod 2^8, z = +311). Class 0 mod 64 has p = 0.6321143, essentially exactly 1-1/e, while the mid-range classes reach 0.6343624.
findings.evidence: lin_S_res.py and lin_T_res2.py, full 2^32 table scans. mod 64: 67,108,864 indices per class, binomial sd 0.0000588, p ranges 0.632114 to 0.634362, max |z| = 26.50 against a Bonferroni threshold of 3.6; the pattern is smooth in the signed residue, lowest near 0 and highest in the middle. Top-6-bit dependence also present, max |z| = 9.71. Finer resolutions: mod 2^8 excess (non-binomial) sd 0.000616, mod 2^12 excess sd 0.000861, mod 2^16 excess sd 0.000440 — it saturates at about 0.14% relative rather than growing.
findings.effect_if_real: Genuinely non-random-map behaviour of sigma0(u)-u, and it is index-side so it is in principle steerable. But the saturated spread means even perfect steering of the index low bits buys under 1% on the lookup survival rate, and nothing at all on the 2^32 fourth-constraint cost. Not a lever.

findings.claim: Defect in the 16 GB table: the value 0x20000000 has exactly one root, u = 0xFFFFFFFF, which is bit-identical to the int32 MISS sentinel (-1), so every lookup of 0x20000000 returns MISS. Any preimage that needs W1, W2 or W3 = 0xFFFFFFFF is unreachable, in both the primary and the root2 table.
findings.evidence: Verified directly: s0(0xFFFFFFFF) = 0x1FFFFFFF, so sigma0(u)-u = 0x20000000; an exhaustive scan of all 2^32 u finds 0xFFFFFFFF is its only root; table[0x20000000] = -1 and root2[0x20000000] = 0xFFFFFFFF. This is also the source of the exact off-by-one between the independent image count (2,721,603,628) and the table's non-sentinel count (2,721,603,627).
findings.effect_if_real: Costs 1 index in 2^32, i.e. 2.3e-10 of the solution space per lookup — cryptanalytically irrelevant, but it is a correctness defect worth fixing (use a separate validity bitmap, or shift the stored value by one) before any exhaustiveness claim is made about the table.

findings.claim: The max-representative distribution of W1, W2, W3 in the corpora is exactly the generic table distribution, and that distribution is exactly the theoretical 'max of a Poisson(1)-conditioned set of uniform 32-bit values'. There is no attack-specific bias in the recovered message words.
findings.evidence: lin_D_table.py / lin_E_cmp.py. Corpus W1/W2/W3 bit means vs 2.53M max-representatives sampled at uniform table indices: max |z| = 2.30 (r19) and 2.59 (r20) over 192 tests, Bonferroni threshold 3.4. The exact full-table bit means of stored representatives are 0.622566, 0.561988, 0.530850, 0.515409, 0.507737, 0.503720, 0.501931, 0.501086 for bits 31 down to 24, with bits 0-23 flat at 0.5000 +- 0.0001. The closed-form prediction for the max of N ~ Poisson(1) | N>=1 uniforms is 1 - E[2^-N] = 0.62254 for bit 31 and 0.56201 for bit 30 — agreement to 4 decimals. W0, W4, a0, a1, e0..e3 are uniform (max |z| <= 2.9 over 20 words).
findings.effect_if_real: Confirms the max policy is the whole story for W-word bias, and that its shape is fully predicted — nothing left over to exploit.

findings.claim: The complete GF(2) affine relation set among the 14 (r19) or 15 (r20) state words per context has dimension 43 (resp. 44), of which 32 are v being constant and the remaining 11 (resp. 12) are all carry-free LSB or bit-1 linearizations of the construction's own modular equations. At R=20 the extra relation is exactly the carry-free bit of the fourth constraint: W3[0] ^ W4[3,7,18] ^ c3[0] = const.
findings.evidence: lin_I_bits.py, exact GF(2) elimination per context on (a0,a1,a2,a3,W0,W1,W2,W3,W4,e0,e1,e2,e3,v[,c3]). Rank 405/448 in every r19 context, 436/480 in every r20 context. Full enumerated list: a0[0]^W0[0]; a0[0,1]^W0[1]; a0[0]^a1[0]^W1[3,7,18]; a2[0]^W1[0]^W2[3,7,18]; a3[0]^W2[0]^W3[3,7,18]; a0[0]^e0[0]; a0[0,1]^e0[1]; a0[0,1]^W0[2]^e0[2]; a0[0,2,13,22]^a1[0]^W1[0]^e0[6,11,25]; a0[2,13,22]^a1[0]^e1[0]; a0[0,1]^a1[1,2,13,22]^a2[0]^W1[4,8,19]^e2[0]; and at R=20 W3[0]^W4[3,7,18]^c3[0]. A modular (Z/2^32) search over 7592 small integer combinations of 12 state words, per-context characteristic function at f=1, found 92 (r19) and 100 (r20) exceedances above a Bonferroni chi2 threshold, every one of which reduces to the forced identities W0 = a0 + C0c, e0 = a0 + Ce0, or the Maj-filter concentration of a2/a3; detection floor per-context |E e^{2pi i T/2^32}| = 0.031 (r19), 0.025 (r20).
findings.effect_if_real: The exact carry-free LSB of the fourth constraint is a genuinely linear 1-bit condition, but it involves W3 and W4 — both post-lookup — so it cannot be pre-satisfied. Nothing else survives.

findings.claim: Data-quality warning on the supplied corpus, and a correction to a false positive it produces: corpus_r20.npz contains 527 duplicated (ctx, a0) pairs (1054 rows, identical c3). These alone manufacture an apparent a0-to-c3 dependence at permutation-calibrated z = +4.2 (64 bins) and z = +10.2 (128 bins); after deduplication the same tests give z = -0.13 and +1.11.
findings.evidence: lin_J_dep.py: 68,680 rows contain 68,152 distinct (ctx,a0) keys; duplicate groups share c3 exactly. The chi2 inflation is quantitatively predicted by 2*b^2/n per duplicate pair (528 pairs x 2*128^2/1717 = 10,086 predicted vs 9,903 observed excess at k=7). Fake-a0 control gives z = -0.85. The generator draws a0 with rng.integers (with replacement), so this is a sampling artifact, not structure.
findings.effect_if_real: Any future mining of these corpora must dedupe on (ctx,a0); effective N for corpus_r20 is 68,152. Two further caveats worth recording: sparse chi2 tables need permutation calibration rather than the asymptotic dof, and stride subsampling of the table (as in multiroot_build.log) biases coverage estimates.

detection_power: All GF(2) rank and nullspace results are exact (integer elimination on every row, no threshold). Statistical thresholds, all Bonferroni-corrected for the number of tests actually run: (1) per-bit distributional tests, sigma = 0.0022 (r19, N=51,268) and 0.0019 (r20, N=68,680), threshold |z| > 3.4 for 192 tests — max observed 2.59, so a per-bit probability bias above 0.0075 would have been seen. (2) Linear-mask correlations a0 -> c3 on the 3.2M-row contiguous sweep: detection floor per-context |corr| = 0.0033, i.e. a bias of 0.0016 in probability, over 2224 mask pairs; on corpus_r20 the same search had a floor of 0.031 per context over 20,000 pairs. (3) c3 uniformity: chi-square on 2^16 low and 2^16 high bins at N = 3.2M gives |z| <= 1.4, and 10,512 Fourier frequencies at N = 68,680 give max |coefficient| 0.0125 against an expected maximum of 0.0116 — so no single frequency could boost P(c3=0) by more than about 1.3%. (4) R=21 joint (c3,c4) independence at N = 1.71e7: MI bound 9.5e-6 bits at 16x16 bins, 1.7e-4 at 64x64; mask search floor |corr| = 0.00061. (5) Maj-filter survival rate: 85.4M lookup-survivors, 8,569 hits, resolution +-1.1% at 1 sigma; per-cell conditional uniformity measured on 2.2M bit-cells. (6) Context-quality dispersion: extra-Poisson relative sd bounded at 0.015 (1 sigma). (3) The mechanism is fully explained, and is generic rather than sigma0-specific. Two measured facts close it: (i) the ball counts are EXACTLY uniform per residue class — 1,048,576 per class mod 4096, measured, and provably so for every modulus 2^k with k <= 14 (for fixed other bits, x = (u_18..u_{17+k}) -> L(u) mod 2^k is unit-lower-triangular hence a bijection, and those bits do not enter the -u term), so the mean preimage count is exactly 1 in every class and the entire hit-rate variation is a pure second-moment effect; (ii) exhaustively at word size 28, the per-class hit rate is explained with R^2 = 0.9948 (corr -0.997) by the per-class variance of the preimage count, which sits just below Poisson (0.9896 vs 1.0). Same scan for other L(u)-u maps at 2^32, all with exactly uniform balls: sigma1-shape spread 0.00505 (max|z| 64.3, and there class 0 is the HIGHEST, not the lowest, so the "lowest near 0" shape is map-specific and not a law), rotr5^rotr11^>>2 spread 0.00317 (|z| 28.8), rotr1^rotr2^rotr3 spread 0.0807 (|z| 1567, hit rate 0.921). Sigma0 is the mildest of the four. "Linear-map-minus-identity mod 2^32 is sub-Poisson and its clumping depends on the low bits of the difference" is a carry-automaton commonplace, not a discovery.

(4) Not steerable, and the ceiling is negligible even granting free steering. Over 200 random contexts x 2^20 random a0, the first lookup index is uniform mod 64 (mean chi2 62.6 on 63 dof, max 92.4 vs Bonferroni-1% ~117) and the per-context predicted first-lookup survival rate has sd 5e-7 — context choice moves it 1000x less than the class spread, so there is no context-selection lever. The only other route is rejecting a0 whose index lands in a bad class, and that is strictly self-defeating: keeping the best 1/256 of mod-4096 classes gives yield/lookup x1.00405 but yield/a0 x0.0039. Under the maximally generous model (index arithmetic free, lookup infinitely dominant) the ceiling is +0.4% on the FIRST lookup only; the second and third indices are not known until their predecessors' lookups have been paid, so they cannot be filtered at all. In the real solver the index costs ~15 ALU ops (S0, S1, Ch, Maj, adds), so the trade is negative. And the representative policy is irrelevant: max vs min changes only which u is stored, never whether an entry exists, so the hit set — and this entire effect — is policy-invariant.

(5) Worth nothing at R=20 regardless: the cost there is the 2^-32 fourth-constraint filter, which this touches by exactly zero.

The reviewer's own bottom line ("Not a lever") is right; what does not survive is the framing as unexplained non-random-map structure. It is explained, generic, already-known in its global form, absent from the data, and its best-case value is +0.4% on one of three lookups under a cost model that does not hold.

verdict:
REFUTED as a lever / as "unexplained structure". Every digit of the claim is CORRECT — I reproduced them independently — but the finding is (a) a restatement of already-known forced structure, and (d) real but useless: it is a single global constant that cannot be conditioned on, steered, or selected, and it is worth +0.0106 bits at R=20.

1. NUMBERS CONFIRMED, INDEPENDENTLY. I wrote my own C full-domain scan (refQ_img.c: 4 GB saturating counter array, no table, no numpy, no shared code with lin_Q_img.py) over all 2^32 u of f(u)=sigma0(u)-u. Exact: image = 2,721,603,628 (0.633672724); >=2 = 1,134,997,809 (0.264262270); >=3 = 341,482,690 (0.079507635); total preimages counted = 2^32 exactly. Identical to the last digit, including the >=2/>=3 counts, which I get WITHOUT their root2/root3 tables. The off-by-one is also confirmed and fully explained: f(0xFFFFFFFF) = 0x20000000 has multiplicity exactly 1, so its unique root IS the sentinel; exactly one key value of 2^32 is lost (2.3e-10). The sweep-survival check also holds: lin_K_seq_big gives 21,348,062/83,886,080 = 0.254489 +- 0.000048, z=+0.91 against p^3=0.254446 and z=+40.1 against (1-1/e)^3=0.252580. So the exact constant is right and the random-map constant is excluded at 40 sigma. Nothing here is a statistical artefact — it is a deterministic fact.

2. THE "MULTIPLICITY DISTRIBUTION" IS ONE NUMBER, NOT THREE. Fit the one-parameter mean-1 under-dispersed family Binomial(m,1/m) to P(0) ALONE: m=119 reproduces the entire exact histogram to <=4e-5 for every k (k=0: 1e-6; k=1: 2.2e-5; k=2: 3.8e-5; k=3: 5.6e-6; ...), and predicts P(>=2)=0.264239 (exact 0.264262, miss 2.3e-5) and P(>=3)=0.079523 (exact 0.079508, miss 1.5e-5), where Poisson misses P(>=3) by 7.9e-4. The reviewer's "P(>=2) sits on Poisson while P(>=1) and P(>=3) do not" is exactly what a one-parameter deformation predicts (dP(>=2)/d(1/m) ~ 0). So "under-dispersion" carries no information beyond the image fraction: it is the same single number said three times. Implied multiplicity variance 0.9916 vs 1.

3. NOT SPECIAL TO sigma0 — GENERIC TO THE MAP CLASS. Full-domain n=32 siblings: sigma0(u)+u gives 0.633672737 (same to 8 digits); sigma1(u)-u gives 0.634894187, i.e. dev +2.77e-3, nearly TWICE sigma0's +1.55e-3. Exhaustive class study of L(u)-u for random invertible GF(2)-linear L: class sd of the image-fraction deviation is 0.0092 (n=18), 0.0066 (20), 0.0043 (22), 0.0026 (24), 0.0024 (26), 0.0011 (28) against true-random-map sampling sd of 6.1e-4 ... 1.9e-5. sigma0's |dev| = 0.00155 at n=32 is a wholly typical member (median |dev| at n=28 is 0.00106). Sparse rotation-shaped L deviate more, up to 0.0146 and -0.125 at n=24. And the deviation shape is one-dimensional across the class: dev(>=3) = -0.460*dev(>=1), r = -0.9994 (resid sd 8.9e-5); sigma0's ratio is -0.511. There IS genuine algebra in the neighbourhood — rank(S0+I)=31 over GF(2), kernel spanned by the sigma0 fixed point 0x27f42515, so sigma0(u) XOR u is exactly 2-to-1 (I measured image = 2^31 exactly) — but that algebra pushes the image DOWN to 0.5; what survives into the subtract world is generic carry noise of the ordinary class size. Nothing unexplained.

4. THE CONSEQUENCE IS PRIOR WORK, AND THE ANOMALY IS NOT ITS SOURCE. "All roots gives 3.93011x" is just 1/p^3 for whatever p is: with the random-map p it is 3.95913x. So the anomaly's own contribution to the headline lever is -0.73%, i.e. the lever exists identically without the finding. Worse, the lever is already logged and already implemented: relx_14_roots.py computes exactly this yield factor, and refuter1_3roots.py runs the 3-table exhaustion end-to-end and MEASURES sol/a0 = 0.9319 over a 2^19 window (vs 0.2545), a factor 3.66x, not 3.93x — 3.93x is the unattainable all-multiplicities-to-14 idealization; the built 3-root tables get 3.66x. The brief also lists the max-representative policy and "reaches only about a quarter of the solutions" as forced, known structure.

5. AND THE GAIN IS PER SWEPT a0, WHICH IS NOT THE COST UNIT. Bookkeeping: max-rep policy does 1+p+p^2 = 2.035 table lookups per swept a0 for 0.2544 candidates = 8.00 lookups/candidate; all-roots does 3.0 lookups per swept a0 for 1.0 candidate = 3.00 lookups/candidate. The real speedup in the dominant cost (random 16 GB accesses) is 2.666x, not 3.93x, and it costs ~3x the table memory. Either way it is a constant factor of 1.4-2.0 bits against a 45.4-bit problem, and it does not touch the fourth constraint.

6. IT CANNOT REDUCE THE RESIDUAL'S ENTROPY, BY CONSTRUCTION. The image/multiplicity structure is a property of the table alone: one global constant, identical for every context, every target and every a0. It is not a function of anything we control, so it fails criterion (i) outright — no per-context selection, no a0-side prediction, no steering. Corpus confirmation of both halves: the corpus W1/W2/W3 carry the max-representative signature (bits 24..31 means 0.505/0.503/0.509/0.507/0.515/0.529/0.562/0.623 for r19 W1, matching the exact whole-table max-rep means 0.5011...0.6226, while W0 is flat at 0.50) — so the "quarter" really is the known policy; and bucketing the r20 residual c3 by the top nibble of W1/W2/W3 gives max |z| = 3.03/3.11/2.81 over 512 bit-tests, below the Bonferroni-5% threshold of 3.9. No linkage.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY WORTH KEEPING: one sentence and one footnote. The constant "about a quarter" should be written 0.254446 (confirmed at 40 sigma against 0.252580 by the 84M-sweep measurement), and the sentinel collision at key 0x20000000 should be noted. That is a correction of 0.0106 bits to a 45.4-bit cost. If someone wants the all-roots factor as a real speedup, the experiment is the one already run and extended: build root4+ tables and re-run refuter1_3roots-style timing end-to-end, reporting wall-clock candidates/second (not candidates/swept-a0) against the max-rep baseline on the same hardware, so the extra random accesses and the 3x table footprint are priced in. My prediction from the bookkeeping is 2.5-2.7x, not 3.93x.
